cards.claim: Decaying learning rate and increasing batch size achieve equivalent training and test performance
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, Wide ResNet-16-4, SGD with momentum 0.9, batch size up to 32000, learning rate decay factor 5
cards.effect: Same test accuracy (~94.3%) and same number of epochs, but batch size increase requires ~2.7x fewer parameter updates (29000 vs 80000)
cards.evidence: Experimental comparison of three schedules: decaying LR, hybrid, and increasing batch size. Figures 2-4 show training curves are nearly identical.
cards.quote: The three training curves are almost identical, despite showing marked drops as we pass through the first two steps (where the noise scale is reduced)... While all three schedules match up to the first "step", after this point increasing the batch size dramatically reduces the number of parameter updates required to train the model.

cards.claim: Noise scale can be reduced by increasing batch size instead of decreasing learning rate
cards.conditions: Theoretical framework based on SDE interpretation of SGD
cards.effect: Equivalent decay in noise scale at constant learning rate, enabling convergence equivalent to learning rate decay
cards.evidence: Theoretical analysis citing Smith & Le (2017) SDE formulation with noise scale = learning_rate / batch_size
cards.quote: However we can achieve the same reduction in noise scale at constant learning rate by increasing the batch size. The main contribution of this work is to show that it is possible to make efficient use of vast training batches, if one increases the batch size during training at constant learning rate

cards.claim: Increasing initial learning rate while scaling batch size further reduces parameter updates
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, Wide ResNet-16-4, initial LR increased from 0.1 to 0.5, initial batch size 640, momentum 0.9
cards.effect: Reduces updates from 29000 to 6500 while maintaining or slightly improving accuracy (94.5% vs 94.2%)
cards.evidence: Experimental comparison across four schedules with different LR and batch size combinations
cards.quote: "Increased initial learning rate" requires under 6500 updates, reaching a final accuracy of 94.5 %. ... Across five additional training runs for each schedule, the median accuracies were 94.3 %, 94.2 %, 94.2 and 93.5 % respectively.

cards.claim: Increasing momentum coefficient while scaling batch size reduces final test accuracy despite fewer parameter updates
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, Wide ResNet-16-4, momentum increased from 0.9 to 0.98, initial batch size 3200
cards.effect: Reduces updates below 2500 but drops accuracy to 93.3% vs 94.3% in baseline, median across 5 runs 93.5%
cards.evidence: Experimental comparison of schedules with different momentum coefficients
cards.quote: Finally "Increased momentum coefficient" requires less than 2500 parameter updates, but reaches a lower test accuracy of 93.3 %.

cards.claim: Accumulation variable during high-momentum training requires additional epochs to stabilize and adapt to loss landscape
cards.effect: Timescale of several epochs for accumulation to forget old gradients; impedes training at points where noise scale decays
cards.evidence: Theoretical analysis in Section 4 with empirical support from Section 5.2
cards.quote: During this time, the magnitude of the parameter updates is suppressed, reducing the rate of convergence. Consequently when training at high momentum one must introduce additional epochs to allow the dynamics to catch up... Once this timescale becomes several epochs long, the accumulation cannot adapt to changes in the loss landscape, impeding training. This is likely to be particularly problematic at points where the noise scale decays.

cards.claim: Increasing batch size from 8192 to 81920 at first noise decay step maintains test accuracy but halves parameter updates
cards.conditions: ImageNet, Inception-ResNet-V2, learning rate 3.0, momentum 0.9, ghost batch size 32, 90 epochs
cards.effect: Test accuracy similar (78.7/77.8 vs 78.1/76.8), parameter updates reduced from 14000 to 6000
cards.evidence: Experimental on larger scale dataset (ImageNet) with more complex architecture
cards.quote: Increasing the batch size reduces the number of parameter updates during training from just over 14000 to below 6000.

cards.claim: Further increasing momentum coefficient to 0.975 while scaling batch size reduces updates below 2500 but drops accuracy on ImageNet
cards.conditions: ImageNet, Inception-ResNet-V2, learning rate 3.0, momentum 0.975, initial batch size 32768, ghost batch size 64
cards.effect: Achieves under 2500 parameter updates but with final accuracies 77.5 and 76.8 (compared to 78.8 with momentum 0.9)
cards.evidence: Experimental comparison of three momentum schedules on ImageNet
cards.quote: Finally "Momentum 0.975" achieves final accuracies of 77.5 and 76.8 in under 2500 updates.

cards.claim: Batch size increase scheduling (8192→16384 after epoch 30) maintains accuracy while reducing total training time on TPU
cards.conditions: ResNet-50 on ImageNet, TPU pod with 256 tensorcores, 90 epochs total
cards.effect: Same validation accuracy 76.1% achieved in 30 minutes instead of 45 minutes; near-perfect scaling efficiency
cards.evidence: Distributed training experiment on specialized hardware (TPU)
cards.quote: Using tensorFlow, we first train ResNet-50 for 90 epochs to 76.1 validation set accuracy in under 45 minutes, utilising batches of 8192 images. To utilise the full TPU pod, we then increase the batch size after the first 30 epochs to 16384 images, and achieve the same validation accuracy of 76.1 in under 30 minutes.

cards.claim: Starting with large batch size throughout training (16384) achieves lower accuracy than ramping up batch size during training
cards.conditions: ResNet-50 on ImageNet, TPU, doubled initial learning rate (0.16), batch size 16384 throughout
cards.effect: Lower validation accuracy 75.0% in 22 minutes, vs 76.1% with batch size ramping
cards.quote: By contrast, doubling the initial learning rate and using batches of 16384 images throughout training achieves a lower validation set accuracy of 75.0 in 22 minutes, demonstrating that increasing the batch size during training is crucial to the performance gains above.

cards.claim: Batch size increase strategy works across multiple optimizers: SGD, SGD with momentum, Nesterov momentum, and Adam
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10, Wide ResNet-16-4, various optimizer configurations
cards.effect: All three schedules (decay LR, hybrid, increase batch) produce equivalent test accuracy curves across all optimizers
cards.evidence: Experimental across Figures 3-4 with different optimizer types
cards.quote: Remarkably, even here the three curves closely track each other. ... We present additional results to establish that our proposal holds for a range of optimizers
